title: Deployment experimentation telemetry hub
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Goal: Build a unified telemetry hub inside Console that makes rollout experiments (canaries, A/B branches, shadow traffic) directly observable and actionable. This hub will surface per-route latency distributions, tail-p99/p999, token-level cost deltas, correctness-signal diffs across cohorts (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE proxies, eval hooks), and trace links to sampled requests. It should enable quick 판단 on whether to promote/cancel/rollback a variant and feed signals into the auto-rollback engine.

Scope: dashboards (overview + cohort diff panel + alert rollup), cohort diff visualizations (time series and distribution diffs), example trace linking to tracing backend, cohort-level error breakdowns (runtime errors, model rejects, rate-limit fallsbacks), and integration with rollout control plane (promote/cancel buttons + canary weight controls). Excludes: full A/B statistical engine internals (ENG will provide APIs), complex causal inference analysis (future work).

Acceptance criteria:
- Console shows a rollout overview page for an active rollout with cohorts listed and live traffic weights.
- Per-route panels report latency p50/p95/p99/p999, token usage, and cost impact per cohort over selectable windows (1m/1h/24h).
- Cohort diff view highlights metric deltas with confidence bands and marks when thresholds for auto-rollback are met.
- Traces sampled from failed or high-latency requests contain cohort metadata and deep-link to tracing UI.
- UI exposes a single-click "Abort variant" that calls the rollout API and records an audit entry.
- Instrumentation documented and an example telemetry ingestion PR merged (see attachments).

Design & trade-offs:
- We will compute cohort diffs server-side (ENG-3421) to avoid browser CPU and to enable consistent aggregation across regions; this requires the rollout service to emit aggregated time-series and distribution sketches. Trade-off: added coupling between rollout controller and metrics pipeline, mitigated by a clear API contract and versioning.
- For latency distributions we will use HDR histograms (compact and fast) instead of raw percentiles to preserve distribution shape in diffs.
- Sampled traces will be limited to error/high-latency buckets to control storage costs; trade-off is less visibility for rare correctness regressions.

Instrumentation plan:
- Metrics emitted from serving runtime: route, model_variant, cohort_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_units, error_kind. (ENG to update schema in ENG-3580).
- Rollout controller aggregates and writes cohort-level time-series to Telemetry store (TSDB) with tags for release and rollback thresholds.
- Console queries new cohort-diff API endpoint for visualizations and subscribes to push updates for active rollouts.

Monitoring & auto-rollback integration:
- Default auto-rollback signals: p99 latency increase > 30% sustained for 10m, error-rate increase > 3% absolute, cost-per-token increase > 50% for 5m. Thresholds configurable per rollout.
- When thresholds hit, Console will show a prominent banner with "Auto-rollback triggered" and a link to audit logs. Backend will execute rollback and emit events consumed by Console.

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Product: Aisha Verma (owner), Priya Natarajan (observability leads)
- Engineering: Liam O'Connor (PM-assignee), Diego Fuentes (runtime), Karen Mills (rollouts service)
- Design: Mei Chen (console UX)

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Large rollouts produce heavy aggregation load on TSDB. Mitigation: enforce sampling and rollup windows, enforce 1-minute granularity for noisy metrics, and offload expensive distribution diffs to a background job.
- Risk: Misleading diffs due to small cohort sizes. Mitigation: show cohort size and confidence intervals, gray out diffs under minimum traffic threshold (default 1000 requests).

Next steps:
- ENG: prototype cohort-diff API and publish schema (ENG-3421) — due 2026-03-20.
- Design: high-fidelity mockups for diff panel and abort UX — due 2026-03-05 (see attachments).
- PM: write rollout playbook text and acceptance tests for SRE runbook — due 2026-03-25.

notes: Do not conflate cohort diffs with long-term feature analytics — this surface is for short-lived rollout decisions.
Consider a follow-up ticket to add hypothesis tracking and statistical test summaries for A/B experiments.
Ensure telemetry retention policy aligns with privacy/compliance; default retention for rollout diffs will be 30 days.
